anti_overlap: Covers Python protocol internals; fd-mcp-tool-schema-discoverability covers MCP surface; fd-cross-connector-fan-out covers multi-connector composition
decision_lens: Does the QueryTemplate protocol follow established patterns (Connector, EntityType, InteractionRule) and handle edge cases those patterns already solved?
focus: Python QueryTemplate ABC design consistency with existing connector/registry patterns
name: fd-query-template-protocol-design
persona: Python API designer who has built plugin registries and protocol-based extension systems
review_areas: QueryTemplate ABC mirrors Connector ABC structure (name, description, typed methods)
TemplateRegistry handles name collision (silent overwrite vs error vs warning)
reset_registry() exists for test isolation (like reset_rules() in rules.py)
execute() return type is a typed QueryResult, not dict[str, Any]
Parameter validation happens before execute(), not inside each template
Templates are stateless — crosswalk/registry injected, not stored

severity_examples.condition: Two plugins register different templates with the same name; last-loaded wins without warning
severity_examples.scenario: Registry silently overwrites templates on name collision

severity_examples.condition: Template registration leaks across test cases causing flaky tests
Callers must defensively check for keys instead of accessing typed fields

success_hints: Template protocol is a natural extension of the existing ABC pattern. Registry has explicit collision handling. Tests can isolate.
task_context: The template layer is the most visible API in interweave — poor protocol design creates friction for every template author and every consumer.
